sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US Food and Drug Administration ordered manufacturers of GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs, including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and Soliqua, to add warning labels about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. NAION is a rare condition caused by reduced blood flow to the optic nerve, which can lead to sudden and permanent vision loss in one eye.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: An FDA review of clinical trials and studies indicated an increased risk of NAION among GLP-1 users. However, Novo Nordisk and the American Academy of Ophthalmology noted that a direct cause-and-effect link has not been established. Patients taking these drugs often already have separate NAION risk factors, such as diabetes and high blood pressure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The American Academy of Ophthalmology advises patients not to stop taking GLP-1 medications without speaking to their doctor, and to consult an ophthalmologist immediately if sudden vision loss occurs.

articles.standfirst: The Prince of Wales says he wants to stop sexual harassment against women in the armed forces.

gist: Prince William has called for better protection from harassment for service women.
A Ministry of Defence survey revealed high rates of unwanted sexualised behaviour.
Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton acknowledged that women's experiences have fallen short.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prince William wrote an article in Country Life stating that current standards do not make everyone feel safe, respected or valued in the military. He held fact-finding meetings with service women across the Army, Royal Navy and the Royal Air Force. A Ministry of Defence survey cited in the article found that 67% of service women faced unwanted sexualised behaviour annually, and 30% considered leaving. The article also mentioned the death of Royal Artillery Gunner Jaysley Beck at Larkhill Camp and allegations from young women at the Army Foundation College at Harrogate.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The intervention highlights ongoing issues with sexualised bullying, harassment and failures in the complaints system within the armed forces, prompting responses from military leadership.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Efforts are being made to create a more positive culture, prevent outdated thinking, and adapt military kit for women.

gist: More than half of surveyed headteachers consider leaving jobs earlier.
Nearly nine in ten reported struggles with mental health and wellbeing.
Teaching unions and Ofsted disagree on the impact of inspections.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A survey by the National Association of Head Teachers found that 52% of responding headteachers are considering cutting short their careers after inspections under Ofsted's new regime. Nearly nine in ten struggled with their mental health and wellbeing, and 64% found the new inspections much more intense than previously.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The findings are described as an unmitigated failure, with school leaders saying the process damages teachers and drives experienced leaders from schools. Teaching unions have declared no confidence in the schools watchdog.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Teaching unions have threatened strike ballots unless significant wellbeing issues are fixed. The education secretary has indicated she is looking at further changes to Ofsted, while Ofsted and the Department for Education say they are working on ways to reduce pressure.
